brief: Bedding. Linen. Actually-breathable stuff made in Portugal. Our customers are mostly people who got tired of the Brooklinen/Parachute aesthetic and want something a little more grown-up.

profile.business_summary: A linen bedding brand, made in Portugal, positioned as breathable and more grown-up than mainstream direct-to-consumer bedding brands.

picks.name: The Affluent Classic
picks.why_plausible: Values "quality and longevity over trends" with home_goods affinity and low price sensitivity, matching premium Portuguese linen at ~$280. Her preference for craftsmanship, heritage and understated tone fits a brand positioned as more grown-up than mainstream DTC.
lean_into: heritage — woven and made in Portugal
quality-focused, linen that lasts and softens with years
picks.ad_angle: Old-world craft: Portuguese-made linen built to outlast trends and soften for decades.

picks.name: The Gifter
picks.why_plausible: The brief lists gift and life_event occasions, and this persona is in-market for "impressive-looking" higher-AOV home goods with low price sensitivity. Linen bedding is a classic wedding/housewarming gift.
lean_into: a gift that looks more expensive than the usual registry pick
picks.ad_angle: The grown-up housewarming/wedding gift: linen bedding that impresses without being obvious.

picks.name: The Wellness Optimizer
picks.why_plausible: Tracks sleep and pays premiums for outcome-focused products; the brief's core claim is "actually-breathable" linen, a direct sleep-quality lever.
lean_into: transparency about the material — pure linen, made in Portugal
breathability as the reason, not a buzzword
avoid: unsupported clinical/science claims the brand can't back
picks.ad_angle: Sleep temperature: linen that actually breathes, for people who wake up hot at 3am.

picks.name: The Sustainability Buyer
picks.why_plausible: Home_goods affinity and willingness to pay more for genuinely made-well goods; European manufacturing and a durable natural fiber are concrete, non-greenwashed claims. Medium price sensitivity is the main risk at $280.
lean_into: specific claim: made in Portugal, not vaguely 'ethically sourced'
linen is a natural fiber that wears for years instead of pilling out
avoid: vague eco language like 'sustainable' with no detail
picks.ad_angle: Known supply chain: one fiber, one country, sheets you won't replace in two years.

creative.angle: Traceable simplicity: one fiber, one country
creative.headline: One fiber. One country: Portugal.
creative.body: Linen bedding made in Portugal. No blends to decode, no vague sourcing — one natural fiber that breathes, and a place you can name.
creative.offer_suggestion: Free swatch set so shoppers can feel the linen before committing at a premium price point
creative.tone_notes: Concrete over adjectival: names the fiber and the country instead of saying 'sustainable' or 'ethically sourced'. No certifications claimed, no durability promises beyond what's stated. Plain, adult tone that matches a skeptical researcher.

creative.angle: Sleep temperature — breathability as the reason, not a buzzword
creative.headline: For the people who wake up hot
creative.body: Linen bedding, made in Portugal. Breathable because of the material, not a finish. Worth a look if temperature is your sleep variable.
creative.offer_suggestion: Free swatch set so she can feel the weight before committing to a full set
creative.tone_notes: Outcome-first and plain: names the 3am overheating problem, then gives the material reason. No clinical or sleep-score claims the brand can't back, no trend talk, no novelty. Transparency reads as spec-sheet honesty, which suits someone who reads labels.

creative.angle: Linen bedding as the grown-up wedding or housewarming gift
creative.headline: A housewarming gift they'll keep
creative.body: Linen bedding, made in Portugal and genuinely breathable. Quieter than the usual registry pick, and it reads that way in the room.
creative.offer_suggestion: Optional gift note or gift box add-on at checkout, if the brand offers one
creative.tone_notes: Frames the purchase as a gift for a wedding or new home rather than self-care, with understated premium language ('quieter', 'reads that way in the room') for a low-price-sensitivity shopper who wants to look tasteful, not flashy. No subscription framing, no urgency.

creative.angle: Old-world Portuguese craft over DTC trend cycles
creative.headline: Portuguese linen, quietly made
creative.body: Linen bedding made in Portugal. Breathable by nature, plain in the best sense, and indifferent to whatever bedding is trending.
creative.offer_suggestion: Free swatch set on request, so she can judge the weave before buying
creative.tone_notes: Understated and craft-led: origin first, no hype words, no influencer or DTC language. 'Quietly made' and 'plain in the best sense' signal grown-up restraint; the trend line stakes out the brief's positioning without naming competitors.

plan.summary: The one true category match (Northbed) is a bedding competitor and stays excluded, leaving a thin plan built on a single premium-home test at Hearthstone Goods while the rest of the catalog is apparel, pet, and grocery inventory with no home-textile intent.

test.name: Hearthstone Goods

signals.name: audience
signals.detail: ages 28-48 cover 72% of 30–55; high income for premium price

test.adjustment_reason: Notes say 'new-home life events drive purchase', a moment when people replace bedding; the category tag only saw kitchen adjacency.
test.rationale: Hearthstone's high-income, 28-48 buyers spending ~$198 on premium kitchen goods are the closest non-competing proxy for design-led home shoppers, and its notes name new-home life events that also trigger bedding replacement.

evidence.quote: Gifting and new-home life events drive purchase

test.risk: Motivation is sustainability and non-toxic cookware rather than aesthetics, so 'made in Portugal' craft messaging may need a durability/natural-fiber angle to land; 2.8M impressions cap the test size.

bid_strategy.rationale: $280 first order (assumed) × 0.30 = $84.00 target CPA: one-time purchase, so the first order has to pay back the acquisition. The max CPA allows headroom while the campaign learns over 14 days.

frequency_cap.rationale: Offers appear once, right after checkout; repeating them reads as spam.

experiment.graduate_rule: After 14 days, move a test publisher to core if its CPA is at or below target; cut any placement above max CPA.
experiment.notes: Creatives rotate evenly until each has enough conversions to compare.

assumptions: We assumed a first order of about $280, typical for a premium linen sheet set.
We assumed the product sells to all genders, ages roughly 30-55.
We assumed one-time purchases rather than a subscription.
Allowable CPA is 30% of first order value (one time); replace with real margin and LTV.
warnings: No publisher cleared the recommended bar, so the whole budget is a test. Treat results as exploratory.
Target CPA is based on an assumed order value. Confirm price before launch.
